questions.q: How did David feel after washing and putting on clean clothes?
choices: Glad to be himself again, yet ashamed of the borrowed clothes
Proud and handsome, and eager to show himself all over the town
Uncomfortable, and wishing he had his old Highland clothes back
Sad, because the new clothes reminded him of his dead father
questions.evidence: I was ashamed of the change too, and, above all, of the borrowed clothes

questions.q: According to Mr. Rankeillor, what did the whole trouble between David's father and uncle hinge on?
choices: A love affair
A gambling debt
A stolen horse
A lost will
questions.evidence: the matter hinges on a love affair

questions.q: What was Ebenezer like when he was young?
choices: Handsome and gallant, so that people stood in doors to watch him
Plain and shy, so that hardly anyone in the country noticed him at all
Clever and studious, the best scholar at the college in his year
Kind and generous, always helping the poor tenants of Shaws
questions.evidence: people stood in their doors to look after him

questions.q: What happened in 1715, when young Ebenezer ran away to join the rebels?
choices: David's father found him in a ditch and brought him back
He fought bravely in a battle and came home a hero
He was taken prisoner and kept for a year in a castle
He sailed off to France and did not come back home for many years
questions.evidence: found him in a ditch, and brought him back

questions.q: How did the two brothers finally settle their quarrel over the lady?
choices: One took the lady, and the other took the estate
They both agreed to give her up and live at Shaws
They fought a duel, and David's father won her hand
Ebenezer married her and gave his brother money
questions.evidence: The one man took the lady, the other the estate

questions.q: Why does Rankeillor think Ebenezer grew so mean and fond of money?
choices: Money was the only thing he got from his bargain, and people shunned him
He had always been poor as a boy and was terribly afraid of ever being poor again
His wife had spent all his money and left him with heavy debts
He was cheated by a lawyer when he was young and trusted no one
questions.evidence: Money was all he got by his bargain

questions.q: What did Rankeillor tell David about his right to the estate?
choices: It was his beyond doubt as heir of entail, whatever his father signed
It belonged to Ebenezer by law because of the bargain that his father had made
It would have to be split evenly between David and his uncle
It had been sold years ago to pay off his uncle's many debts
questions.evidence: you are the heir of entail

questions.q: Why did Rankeillor not want to take the case to court?
choices: Witnesses might let slip something about Mr. Thomson
The judges were all good friends of Ebenezer
David was too young to bring a lawsuit at all
The court would take ten years or more to decide it
questions.evidence: some word of your friend Mr. Thomson must certainly crop out

questions.q: What was Rankeillor's first reaction to David's plan, since it meant meeting Mr. Thomson?
choices: He said it was inadmissible, but kept thinking about it all through dinner
He agreed at once and sent Torrance off to find Alan hiding in the fields by the road
He laughed and said it was the best plan he had ever heard
He grew angry and told David to leave his house that night
questions.evidence: I am afraid your scheme is inadmissible

questions.q: Why did Rankeillor ask his clerk, Torrance, to come along?
choices: He would probably be wanted as a witness
He knew the path to the House of Shaws
He was to carry a pistol to guard them all
He was an old friend of Uncle Ebenezer
questions.evidence: you will probably be wanted as a witness

questions.q: What funny story did Rankeillor keep telling again and again over the wine?
choices: How he once failed to know his own clerk for lack of spectacles
How Ebenezer once fell off his horse in front of the whole town
How he once got lost on the road to Queensferry in a fog
How a big dog once ran off with his best powdered wig at the market
questions.evidence: I did not know my own clerk

questions.q: Why had Rankeillor really "forgotten" his glasses?
choices: So he could never swear he had recognised Alan
So he would have an excuse to lean on David's arm
So that Torrance would have to read the deed aloud
So that Ebenezer would think he was a harmless old man
questions.evidence: it had been done on purpose

questions.q: What did David feel as they passed the Hawes Inn and the Ferry pier?
choices: Sorrow for those lost since that day, and a chill of remembered fear
Anger at the landlord, who he believed had helped the captain to kidnap him that day
Joy that he would soon be sailing away on another ship
Nothing at all, because he did not recognise the place
questions.evidence: I could not behold the place without sorrow for others and a chill of recollected fear

questions.q: How did David find Alan when they came near the meeting place?
choices: He whistled the Gaelic air and Alan answered it
He called out Alan's name loudly into the dark
He saw the glow of Alan's pipe behind a dyke
He followed Alan's footprints up from the sea-shore
questions.evidence: I went up the hill, whistling from time to time my Gaelic air

questions.q: Why did Alan answer Rankeillor so stiffly when the lawyer said he might pass him by tomorrow?
choices: His pride was hurt
He did not trust lawyers
He was very hungry
He disliked the plan
questions.evidence: the Highlandman's vanity was ready to startle at a less matter than that

questions.q: Why was it good that there was no light in the House of Shaws when they arrived?
choices: It meant Uncle Ebenezer was already in bed
It meant the house was empty and unlocked
It meant no soldiers were waiting inside
It meant the servants had all gone home
questions.evidence: It seemed my uncle was already in bed

questions.q: What did Alan do once the others were hidden by the corner of the house?
choices: Strode openly to the door and began to knock
Climbed in through a window at the back
Fired his pistol into the air to wake Ebenezer
Called up to the tower in a loud Highland voice
questions.evidence: Alan strode to the door without concealment and began to knock

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David learns his family's secret and joins the lawyer and Alan in a plan against his uncle
David and Mr. Rankeillor take Uncle Ebenezer to the court in Edinburgh and win the whole case there
Alan is arrested on the road to Shaws, and David must find a way to rescue him
David decides to give up the estate and go away to France with Alan Breck
questions.evidence: I began to see the outlines of that scheme on which we afterwards acted
